rows.reason: All four PASS in verdicts.json ('empty backdrop, look held, props as asked'); seen on this sheet: one drawn world, no people, strong readable props. rows.route: J2/J4 first frames (hero placed in a place by reference)
rows.made_for: Question C: does the hero survive a change of environment when Qwen places him in a backdrop by reference (seeds 11 and 23)?
rows.reason: Answer on record: the environment change did not break the hero (CLIP cosine .78-.82 against the front sheet; the ship at seed 11 is weakest, .70: shorter beard, softer face). Seen on the sheet: face, scar, beard, fur and armour are kept, but pose and boots drift, the pose is a stiff centred stand, scale differs between the two seeds, and in the tent at seed 11 the campfire of the backdrop is gone while seed 23 keeps it (the model may delete backdrop props).
rows.not_verified: why the fire disappears at seed 11 was not investigated

Panorama (nomadoor outpaint LoRA, licence qwen-research): horizon continues, seam scores 1.76/1.66 (a TEST row, not a pass).

rows.reason: The first round showed the whole set in every camera because the brief did not list what the clip needs; the in_shot round (this sheet) fixes that. rows.route: J4 family (crowd), stage 1 of the pilot and P1
rows.cost: US$0 (5,000 Quaternius soldiers; colour 202.3 s/frame, depth 238.1 s/frame)
rows.made_for: The 11-still contact sheet of the pilot minute: seven room stills plus battle frame 0, frame 200, wide high and front mid.
rows.reason: Good as layout and crowd composition (thousands of agents, banners, two armies), weak as a picture. Battle frame 0 is from behind the front rank, so it shows no faces and no commander; wide high and front mid are taken at frame 112, just before contact, and the baked crowd has no real collision (the wedge passes through the wall after about frame 130), so LTX would have to invent the clash. The soldiers repeat one template.

rows.reason: Good: identity and the world are exactly the approved sheet and plate, the cut is free and fast, the 180-degree rule and eye-lines hold. Bad (the creator's own reading, 2026-11-06): the man in the picture is not good enough because too few reference frames were supplied; seen here: H1 exists only as a belt-up card from two sheets (left34, back), the reverse shot uses the back sheet mirrored, the close-up is the same card enlarged and soft, and no mouth or blink variants exist. Backgrounds in the over-the-shoulder shots are heavily blurred plate crops.
